conventions.convention: The presentation has standard two-form ω=Σ dqᵃ∧dpₐ, Hamiltonian convention ι_XH ω=dH, and observable evolution {f,H}.
Hamilton–Jacobi solutions are C³ functions S(t,q,α) on nonempty open domains, for a C² chart Hamiltonian, satisfying S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0; S has action dimension.
Completeness means det S_qα≠0 at the specified base point; p=S_q and β=S_α. Parameters α have configuration-coordinate dimensions, so β has momentum-type dimensions.

A completely integrable datum has n smooth functions F₁=H on a nonempty open 2n-dimensional momentum domain, pairwise commuting and differentially independent on a dense open subset. A regular value belongs to the image and is regular at every preimage.

The torus and action-angle statements assume countable choice, a nonempty compact connected regular fibre, and a saturated neighbourhood over a ball where the integral map is a proper submersion with connected fibres.
Action-angle angles have period one, ω=Σ dθᵢ∧dIᵢ, and cyclic frequencies ∂h/∂Iᵢ. Radian coordinates are θrad=2πθ and Irad=I/(2π). Additive action constants are not fixed by the theorem.
The oscillator example fixes I=∮p dx, while the Kepler radial example uses the radian action Jₐ=(1/π)∫sqrt(2μ(E−Ueff)) dρ, so Jₐ′=T/(2π).

The adiabatic estimate uses a fixed time-independent radian canonical chart, C² open extension data, a frequency lower bound, and explicit compact trapping throughout [0,A/ε]. The slow parameter is dimensionless and ε has inverse-time dimension.

Kepler calculations invoke gravitational-model clause (i), retain gravitational couplings distinct from inertial masses, assume J>0, and apply the simple-turning-point action theorem only on the noncircular energy window.

load_bearing.statement: F=(F₁,…,Fₙ), Fᵢ:W₀→R, consists of C∞ phase functions with F₁=H|W₀, pairwise in involution and with linearly independent differentials on a dense open subset of W₀.

Under countable choice, complete integrability, a nonempty compact connected regular fibre, and the stated saturated proper-submersion neighbourhood with connected fibres, a shrunk saturated neighbourhood admits period-one action-angle coordinates with ω=Σ dθᵢ∧dIᵢ; fibrewise-constant smooth functions depend only on I, H=h(I), and the stated linear-motion and radian-rescaling conclusions hold.
A C³ Hamilton–Jacobi solution S is a complete integral at (t₀,q₀,α₀) when det S_qα(t₀,q₀,α₀)≠0; its attached maps are p=S_q and β=S_α.

A C³ complete integral for the chart's C² Hamiltonian produces local Hamiltonian characteristic curves, constant β=S_α, a local converse solving β=S_α for q, and local canonical labels with ω=dβ∧dα. Its Statement distinguishes Cartesian model motions from generalized-coordinate solutions of the substituted Lagrange equations.

Under its stated hypotheses, N is an embedded n-dimensional Lagrangian submanifold spanned by the Hamiltonian fields; their restricted commuting flows generate a transitive Rⁿ action with a common full stabilizer lattice Γ, and N is diffeomorphic to Tⁿ.
For the stated trapped branch on [0,A/ε], |I(t)−I(0)|≤ε[2 sup|g|+A sup|g_I k_θ−g_θ k_I−g_s|], with suprema over K×[0,2π]×S₀ and g=(k−〈k〉)/h_I.

concerns.concern: Statement clause 4 and F6 identify Hamiltonian solutions with 'the model’s motions' in every allowed momentum chart, citing clause 1 of pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations. That supplier's clause 1 is Cartesian; clause 2 gives only the substituted Lagrange equations for generalized-coordinate maps. The allowed maps include lower-dimensional immersions without an ideal-constraint hypothesis. For example, take one ambient particle, X(q)=(q,q²,0), U(x)=k x₁²/2 and d=0. The substituted Hamiltonian P²/[2m(1+4q²)]+kq²/2 has compact connected regular positive-energy fibres and proper nearby energy bands. At q=0, P≠0, its reconstructed curve has x₂″=2(P/m)², although the ambient force has zero second component. Thus the structural action-angle conclusion is sound, but the asserted model-motion identification is false at the stated immersion scope.

The introductory parenthesis says 'motions of the model are the integral curves of the branch Hamiltonian field, in each chart', and clause (b) states the corresponding equivalence without distinguishing full-dimensional charts from lower-dimensional immersions. Its supplier proves only substituted Lagrange-equation equivalence in the latter case. The parabolic immersion X(q)=(q,q²,0) with ambient U=kx₁²/2 demonstrates that a substituted Hamiltonian solution need not reconstruct an unconstrained model motion.

The Statement correctly distinguishes Cartesian model motions from generalized-coordinate solutions of the substituted Lagrange equations, but physical_scope says that on the potential branch the characteristic curves 'are motions of the model' without that distinction. The A-page summary repeats the broader model-motion reading. Lower-dimensional immersion reconstruction requires additional physical hypotheses; the public scope should agree with the qualified Statement.

Clause (c) states the bracket criterion as an iff and says 'The equivalence is clause 2 of pthm-cm13-observable-evolution'. The cited clause proves only bracket vanishing implies constancy along a solution. The reverse direction follows by taking a local Hamiltonian solution through every point and differentiating at its initial time, using local existence, but this direction is not supplied by the cited clause.

Claims 1 and 3 invoke the physical CM14 definitions and theorems for a scalar Cartesian phase plane. Those definitions begin with the force branch Q⊂R^(3N), N≥1, or a declared generalized-coordinate immersion into that branch. The harmonic postulate instead adopts a separately declared scalar model class, explicitly not derived from the three-dimensional branch. No scalar extension of the CM12–CM14 interfaces or ambient embedding is specified here. The displayed calculations are correct, but the claimed instance of the physical definitions is not established at their exact domain.

Given calls W=R² the Cartesian phase domain of pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity, and L1 calls (H) a datum of def-cm14-complete-integrability. The cited Cartesian presentation has dimension 6N for N≥1, while the harmonic postulate is a separately adopted scalar class. No permitted scalar extension or declared immersion identifies this witness with the physical datum class being refuted. The point-versus-circle computation is correct, but the witness's membership in the stated class is unsupported.

The complete-integral claim uses the same unstated scalar extension of the CM14 physical definitions as the companion oscillator example. post-cm04-harmonic-model supplies scalar dynamics, whereas def-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-equation fixes a three-dimensional force presentation or its explicitly declared immersion. Supply that identification before applying the physical complete-integral interface.

Step 3.2 applies the inverse-function/FTC substitution through the turning endpoints, where ρ′=0 and the inverse time derivative is singular. thm-substitution requires an everywhere differentiable compact-interval substitution with integrable derivative and continuous outer integrand. The intended argument works on interior truncations followed by endpoint limits; convergence is already provided by thm-cm-action-variable-derivative. Those truncations and limits should be stated.

The initial motion is x:I→Q on an arbitrary model interval, but L2 and step 4.1 use θ:R→R and full periods without explicitly passing to the global central-force extension supplied by thm-cm-kepler-orbit-period. The physical period supplier distinguishes the global coordinate extension from its restriction to the prescribed model time window. Name that extension when invoking the global period argument.

Status clause (d) reads 'It asserts that no particular model of the force branch is completely integrable, that no fibre is compact, connected or a torus…'. Grammatically this asserts negative mathematical claims, rather than saying that the definition asserts none of those properties. The intended nonassertion should be stated directly.

alerts.finding: Proof step 1.1 writes 'dF_j(X_{F_i})=ω(X_{F_j},X_{F_i})=−{F_j,F_i}=0'. The published bracket definition gives {F_j,F_i}=ω(X_{F_j},X_{F_i}), with no minus sign. Involution makes the final zero valid, and the batch's regular-tori proof uses the correct sign, but the displayed intermediate identity is wrong.

Step 5.2 says 'Its pullback τ=σ*ω is closed. On the ball [F4] gives τ=dα.' F4 cites thm-poincare-lemma-for-star-shaped-domains, whose Statement supplies a scalar potential for a closed C¹ vector field, equivalently a one-form primitive. It does not supply a one-form primitive for the closed two-form τ. The local mathematical supplier thm-cm-liouville-arnold-action-angle-repaired explicitly closes this gap using a separate two-form primitive and is the theorem consumed by this batch.

The notation paragraph says 'the integral is twice the momentum phase-space area'. If p₊=sqrt(2m(E−U(q))), the enclosed momentum phase-plane area is 2∫p₊ dq. The displayed action Jₐ=(1/π)∫p₊ dq is area/(2π); the unnormalised displayed integral is half the area, not twice it. The defining formula and this batch's normalization are correct.

The first remark says 'ACω enters only in the counterexample sequence of step 4.1'. The repaired theorem also consumes the lattice and compact-flow suppliers, whose current Statements explicitly assume ACω; its own final remark acknowledges those uses. The choice-cost description omits the inherited compact-flow/lattice uses.

The page says pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations 'identifies the integral curves … with the momentum-phase curves of the model’s motions, in every chart'. Its clause 1 gives Cartesian model-motion equivalence; clause 2 gives substituted Lagrange-equation equivalence for arbitrary generalized-coordinate maps. Lower-dimensional immersions require the separate ideal-constraint hypotheses for reconstruction as constrained model motions. The page's unrestricted summary is stronger than its supplier.
